must_remember: According to Rayleigh criterion, two point sources are just resolved when the central maximum of one diffraction pattern coincides with the first minimum of the other.
The angular separation for a circular aperture is given by $d\theta = 1.22 \frac{\lambda}{D}$.
Resolving power of a telescope is directly proportional to objective diameter $D$ and inversely proportional to wavelength $\lambda$.
Resolving power of a microscope depends on numerical aperture ($n \sin \theta$) and wavelength $\lambda$ through the relation $\Delta x = \frac{\lambda}{2n \sin \theta}$.
Resolving power of a diffraction grating is given by $R = \frac{\lambda}{d\lambda} = N n$, where $N$ is the total number of lines and $n$ is the order of spectrum.
Magnification does not improve the optical resolution of an instrument; resolution is strictly governed by wave optics parameters.

glossary.meaning: The central bright diffraction disk formed when light from a point source passes through a circular aperture.
The product $n \sin \theta$, characterizing the acceptance angle and light-gathering power of a microscope objective.
The ability of an optical instrument to distinguish closely spaced point objects or adjacent spectral lines as separate entities.
The sum of the width of a ruling and the width of an opaque space ($a$), representing the spatial period of a diffraction grating.
